supporting_observations.claim: The repeated HTTPS checks in the alerted period went to update.stockpilot.com through the explicit proxy and are attributed by endpoint network telemetry to C:\Program Files\StockPilot\stockpilotupd.exe (PID 4108), running as eli.brooks.

The updater's observed checks recur at roughly five-minute intervals: 13:40:41, 13:45:59, 13:50:21, 13:55:20, 14:00:16, 14:05:54, and 14:10:40 UTC. This matches the inventory description that StockPilot checks update.stockpilot.com about every five minutes.
The 14:00:16 proxy attempt received status 407 (auth-required), while the other listed StockPilot attempts received status 200; the 407 record does not show a successful tunnel.

Endpoint network events independently attribute multiple successful proxy connections to update.stockpilot.com checks to the StockPilot updater process, corroborating that the periodic traffic is the approved updater rather than an unidentified process.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT destinations, status, byte counts, and tunnel metadata; the available evidence does not show the HTTPS request or response contents for the StockPilot checks.
The supplied records do not establish the updater executable's hash, signature, or whether any update payload was downloaded or executed.
claims_not_established: The content or integrity of any data exchanged inside the successful StockPilot TLS tunnels.
Whether the updater downloaded or installed an update during this interval.
Whether the updater binary is authentic; the supplied records identify its path and process but do not provide signature or hash verification.
unrelated_findings: Cisco AnyConnect's VPN UI was launched by eli.brooks at 14:04:36 and loaded a signed Cisco DLL. The inventory states there is no VPN; these records show a launch, not a VPN connection. Review separately. (T206-00194, T206-00195, T206-00196)

FILE-BLU-01 at 10.54.20.20 queried WS-EBROOKS-01 and then made a TCP connection to the workstation on port 9997 that ended with RSTR; the available records do not identify the service or explain the connection. Review separately. (T206-00283, T206-00284, T206-00285)

UserAssist registry records contain encoded paths that decode to mstsc.exe and powershell.exe. These are outside the alerted HTTPS activity and are not, by themselves, proof of malicious execution; review separately if warranted. (T206-00127, T206-00187)
